subject.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)

question: Should OpenClaw treat full-line `antml:`/`mm:` or `<function_calls>`-wrapped invoke XML outside Markdown code as disposable leaked tool-call text in persisted assistant history, even when it could be intentional provider-authored prose?
rationale: The implementation is internally consistent and tested, but the acceptable false-positive policy for irreversible transcript sanitization is not established by an existing public contract or test alone.

options.title: Preserve qualified text in history
options.body: Scrub the qualified markup from user-visible delivery but retain it in durable assistant history until a stronger provider-origin signal can distinguish leaks from intentional content.

options.title: Adopt qualified-form deletion
options.body: Land the branch’s current rule and explicitly accept that namespace-qualified full-line XML outside code regions is reserved for degraded tool-call leakage.

options.title: Define a new durable-text contract first
options.body: Pause the PR while maintainers document a provider-origin or transcript-sanitization contract that can support a less ambiguous persisted-history rule.

recommendation.title: Preserve qualified text in history
recommendation.body: Scrub the qualified markup from user-visible delivery but retain it in durable assistant history until a stronger provider-origin signal can distinguish leaks from intentional content.

likelyOwner.reason: The author has the most complete documented explanation of the proposed classification boundary and can clarify the implementation trade-off; final product acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
